### SVBONY

Devices: Camera.

- The camera driver accepts a non-owning `SVBSDK` seam; any injected SDK must outlive the driver and the exposure body its `util::CaptureSession` joins ([decision 0020](../../docs/decisions/0020-capture-session.md), #1980). Extend `fake_svbony_sdk.h` and its connected contract/stress coverage when changing acquisition behavior.
- **Exposure body** (#1980): the Exposure register write, the deferred ROI and `FrameSpeedMode` writes, the readback checks, `SVBStartVideoCapture` (with `CaptureControl::exposure_started()` just before it), the 500 ms `SVBGetVideoData` reads (each read is the poll step; the body has no sleep of its own) and `SVBStopVideoCapture` on every way out run in the session body, so a StartExposure while one runs is `InvalidOperation` and the register is never written under a live capture. AbortExposure and a Disconnect mark the exposure stopping and call the SDK stop under `mutex_` before the session joins the body; a stop that fails sets `capture_stop_failed_` and fails the exposure with the "capture stop was not confirmed" text, so `CameraState` reads Idle and `ImageReady` raises it until the next StartExposure or a reconnect. StartExposure and the settings writers refuse with `DriverException` while `capture_stop_failed_` is set, and an AbortExposure with nothing exposing retries the stop. A body's own stop result never overwrites a newer one AbortExposure or a Disconnect recorded (`capture_stop_epoch_`).
- **Link loss** (#1986, [decision 0009](../../docs/decisions/0009-link-loss-and-relink-policy.md)): every post-connect device call (control reads and writes, pulse guide, and every SDK call of the exposure body) goes through `on_link()`. `NotConnected` from the call, which the wrapper makes of `SVB_ERROR_CAMERA_REMOVED` and `SVB_ERROR_CAMERA_CLOSED` only, is a lost link at once: `Connected` reads false (a `util::LinkEpoch`), members throw `NotConnected` with the SDK text, which `get_link_fault()` also gives until the next Connect or Disconnect, one WARN names the serial, the exposure in flight fails with that text and makes no further read, and the dead handle is closed (by the exposure body on its way out when one is running). `SVB_ERROR_INVALID_ID` stays `InvalidValue` and is not evidence; a timeout or a generic error keeps the link; there is no failed-read latch, staleness bound or `LinkLostStamp`. Only the client relinks: a Connect after a loss joins the body the loss left and opens the camera afresh by `camera_index_`; a Disconnect of a lost camera completes, and a removal code from the Disconnect's own SDK close is logged and swallowed (any other close error surfaces). Whether a real cable pull returns a removal code is unverified on hardware (no SVBONY camera on the rig); the ZWO camera precedent is a pull that returns a generic error, which this driver does not detect. `lost_mutex_` is a vendor-local leaf under `mutex_` (the loss reason and the unit label).

SDK location: `AlpacaCore/external/SVBONY/lib/armv8/`, headers under `external/SVBONY/include/`.

- **Keep the static SDK's symbols private.** `libSVBCameraSDK.a` bundles libusb; its INTERFACE `--exclude-libs` link option prevents those definitions from replacing shared SDKs' USB dependencies. HTTP must propagate that option through PRIVATE static dependencies (`CMP0099` NEW, set by its CMake 3.18 minimum), not just to the directly linked Core tests. The [#1211 matched rig comparison](../../docs/qhy-usb-recovery.md) records the stable-based control failure and isolated QHY reconnect successes, with stale-descriptor retention still unresolved. Keep both symbol-isolation CTests when changing this link path.

- **SC715C is a rebadged ToupTek G3M715C, NOT served by this driver.** The SVBONY SDK does not recognize the SC715C. Configure it with vendor `touptek` (device type Camera, `ALPACACORE_ENABLE_TOUPTEK`) — the ToupTek SDK enumerates it natively under its own model name `G3M715C`. Same rebadge pattern as the iOptron iCAM cameras being served by the Player One driver (see [iOptron notes](ioptron.instructions.md)) -- but with one difference that matters to the user: the router aliases vendor `ioptron` + camera onto the Player One driver, so an iCAM owner still selects `ioptron`. There is no `svbony` + camera alias (that vendor has its own driver), so the SC715C must be configured as `touptek`. Validated 2026-09-11 on Linux arm64: 0 errors, 0 issues, 0 timing issues (ConformU 4.5.1 — see the [ConformU 4.5.0 arm64 timing bug](testing.instructions.md#conformu-version-arm64-timing-bug) note if an earlier ConformU version shows spurious timing failures). Report saved at `AlpacaCore/conformu/SVBONY/SC715C/Linux-arm64.txt`.

- **Control warm-up at connect (SV905C2 quirk)**: After `SVBOpenCamera`, `SVBSetControlValue(SVB_GAIN, ...)` returns `SVB_ERROR_GENERAL_ERROR` indefinitely on SV905C2 — regardless of value, regardless of `bAuto` flag, regardless of whether `SVBStartVideoCapture` is active, and `SVBRestoreDefaultParam` does not clear the state. The driver works around this by iterating every writable control reported by `SVBGetControlCaps` and writing each to its `default_value` during the connect path (after `SVBSetROIFormat` / `SVBSetOutputImageType`). Once any `SVBSetControlValue` call has landed, subsequent client gain writes succeed. Failures during the warm-up are tolerated and logged at DEBUG. Do not remove the warm-up loop in `set_connected` without re-running ConformU against an SV905C2 — the failure is silent until a client tries to set gain. Likely related to SDK readme entries `v1.13.1: Fixup ASCOM software to support SV905C2` and `v1.13.2: Optimize gain settings of SV905C2`.
- **Auto control writes**: `disable_auto_if_needed` reads the current value/auto flag and only writes back if currently auto, since some SVBONY models reject manual writes while auto is active with the same `SVB_ERROR_GENERAL_ERROR`.
- **`SVBSetControlValue` retry**: The wrapper retries up to 3 times with a 50 ms backoff specifically on `SVB_ERROR_GENERAL_ERROR` to absorb genuinely transient hardware-op faults; deterministic rejections still surface after the retries are exhausted.
- **Camera mode**: We use `SVB_MODE_NORMAL` (continuous video) and start/stop `SVBStartVideoCapture` per exposure. INDI's `indi-svbony` driver instead uses `SVB_MODE_TRIG_SOFT` with persistent video capture for stills — keep this in mind if a future SVBONY model needs trigger-mode behavior.
- **Acquisition timing** (issue #1477): candidate duration is the rounded/clamped exposure register in microseconds; UTC and TaskClock progress start at `StartVideoCapture` after deferred ROI/speed writes. The SDK's stale-frame flushing and sensor-start latency still need hardware evidence; do not invent a frame-discard count.
- **Bin/ROI quirks**: divisors width%8, height%2 (see [Camera ROI alignment](ascom-contract.instructions.md#camera-roi-alignment-all-camera-vendors)). ROI updates and `FrameSpeedMode` writes are deferred to `start_exposure` because some SDK control writes take ~1.1 s and would otherwise blow ASCOM client timing budgets.
- **`SVBRestoreDefaultParam`** is called immediately after `SVBOpenCamera` to clear any leftover state from a previous session, mirroring `indi-svbony`. Tolerate failure for older SDK builds that don't export the symbol.
